draft.title: The end of apartheid
card: Apartheid was the system of racial separation and white minority rule in South Africa. It was enforced by law from 1948 and denied the Black majority political rights.
Protest inside
Black South Africans, with allies of other groups, resisted through strikes, school and community protests, and the African National Congress (ANC). The government often answered with force and bans.
Pressure from abroad
Other countries and groups used sanctions (trade and financial penalties) and sporting boycotts. These raised the cost of keeping apartheid.
Outcome
Under growing pressure, the government freed Nelson Mandela in 1990 and held talks with the ANC. South Africa's first elections open to all races were held in 1994, and Mandela became president.
draft.remember: Apartheid ended because protest at home and pressure from abroad pushed the government to negotiate.

a.q: Which action is an example of pressure from abroad on South Africa's apartheid government?
opts: Other countries placing sanctions on South African trade
ANC supporters joining strikes in South African cities
Students in Soweto protesting about their schooling
South Africa's government banning protest groups
a.why: Sanctions were imposed by other countries to make apartheid costly to keep. The strikes and student protests were protest inside South Africa, and bans were the government's own response.
a.clue: Look for action taken by people outside South Africa.

b.q: Which statement best explains why South Africa held elections open to all races in 1994?
opts: Protest and outside pressure pushed the government to negotiate
Sanctions alone made protest inside South Africa unnecessary
The government gave up apartheid before any protest began
Mandela's release in 1990 came before any talks with the ANC
b.why: The card links the end of apartheid to protest at home and pressure from abroad together, which led to Mandela's release, talks and the 1994 vote. The option about sanctions alone is tempting, but it ignores protest inside South Africa.
b.clue: The change came from more than one source of pressure.
